title: A finite inverse tetrahedron detects equivalences
statement:
Use quasicategories, equivalence edges, and standard simplices from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Form the simplicial set
$$Q=\Delta^0\amalg_{\Delta^{\{0,2\}}}\Delta^3\amalg_{\Delta^{\{1,3\}}}\Delta^0,$$
collapsing each displayed opposite edge to a vertex, and write $c:\Delta^1\to Q$ for the image of the central edge $\{1,2\}$. For every small quasicategory $D$ and every equivalence edge $e:\Delta^1\to D$, there is a simplicial map $f:Q\to D$ with $fc=e$. Every simplicial map $Q\to D$ carries every edge of $Q$ to an equivalence in $D$.

source.place: Higher Algebra, proof of Proposition B.1.6, forward direction (3) and reverse direction (A1), printed pp.1473-1474. The first assertion is the extension of the central edge into the Kan core; the second is the inverse diagram chase. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical fact.
